def toggle_core(
    current_frame: Any,
    transitions: list[dict[str, Any]],
    act: Callable[..., None],
    trace: list[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Lights-out core: rebuild click stencils from the observed transitions,
    GF(2)-solve for a uniform board and queue the plan; if there are not yet
    enough stencils (<_MIN_STENCILS), queue the next systematic probe click.

    Added fallback: when the linear system is inconsistent (e.g. because the
    game does not follow a global linear toggle rule), we greedily click any
    cell that is currently on using the learned per‑click stencils (or the cell
    itself as a best‑effort guess). This prevents the solver from stalling on
    games where each click toggles only its own cell or where the toggle pattern
    is state‑dependent.
    """
    frame = np.asarray(current_frame)
    stencils = _stencils_from_transitions(transitions)

    # If we have enough distinct stencils, attempt the linear‑algebraic solve.
    if len(stencils) >= _MIN_STENCILS:
        plan = _solve_board(frame, stencils, trace)
        if plan:
            if trace is not None:
                trace.append(f"plan={len(plan)} clicks")
            for (x, y) in plan:
                act("CLICK", x, y)
            return

        # Linear solve failed (plan is None). Try a greedy fallback.
        bits, _off, _on = _binarize(frame)

        # If the board is already uniform, nothing to do.
        if np.all(bits == bits.flat[0]):
            return

        # Build a mapping from each toggled cell to a click that toggles it.
        cell_to_click: dict[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int]] = {}
        for click, cells in stencils.items():
            for (r, c) in cells:
                # Prefer the first observed click for a given cell.
                cell_to_click.setdefault((r, c), click)

        # Greedy plan: click a known click for each cell that is currently ON.
        fallback_plan_set: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
        on_coords = np.argwhere(bits == 1)
        for r, c in on_coords:
            # Use the observed click if we have one; otherwise guess the cell itself.
            click = cell_to_click.get((r, c), (c, r))
            fallback_plan_set.add((int(click[0]), int(click[1])))

        if fallback_plan_set:
            fallback_plan = list(fallback_plan_set)
            if trace is not None:
                trace.append(f"fallback plan={len(fallback_plan)} clicks")
            for (x, y) in fallback_plan:
                act("CLICK", x, y)
            return

    # Either we have too few stencils or both the linear solve and fallback
    # produced no actionable plan – fall back to systematic probing.
    probe = _next_probe(frame, set(stencils))
    if probe is not None:
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(
                f"stencils={len(stencils)} (<{_MIN_STENCILS}) -> "
                f"probe ({probe[0]},{probe[1]})"
            )
        act("CLICK", probe[0], probe[1])

def paint_core(
    current_frame: Any,
    transitions: list[dict[str, Any]],
    act: Callable[..., None],
    trace: list[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Paint/flood core: infer the fill colour from observed click transitions;
    once confirmed, queue clicks filling the largest remaining background regions;
    before it is confirmed, queue one probe click to elicit the mechanic.

    The original inference logic compared the dominant new colour against the
    total number of changed cells, which broke when a click also altered
    non‑background cells (e.g. a UI element).  The updated logic only
    considers cells that were background before the click and requires the
    dominant new colour to dominate *among those* background‑changed cells.
    This reliably detects the fill colour even when auxiliary cells change
    alongside the fill.
    """
    # Convert the current frame to a NumPy array for processing.
    frame = np.asarray(current_frame)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Infer the fill colour from the transition history.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    votes: dict[int, int] = {}
    for t in transitions:
        # Only consider transitions that resulted from a click.
        if t.get("xy") is None:
            continue

        before = np.asarray(t["before"])
        after = np.asarray(t["after"])

        # Shapes must match; otherwise the transition is irrelevant.
        if before.shape != after.shape:
            continue

        # Determine which cells changed.
        diff = before != after
        if not diff.any():
            continue

        # Mask of cells that were background before the click and changed.
        bg_mask = (before == _BACKGROUND) & diff
        if not bg_mask.any():
            # No background cells were affected – this click does not reveal the
            # fill mechanic.
            continue

        # New colours of the background‑changed cells.
        new_vals, new_counts = np.unique(after[bg_mask], return_counts=True)

        # Require the most common new colour to dominate among the background‑changed cells.
        # Using 60 % of the background‑changed cells (instead of all changed cells)
        # makes the inference robust when auxiliary cells also change.
        if int(new_counts.max()) >= 0.6 * bg_mask.sum():
            top_color = int(new_vals[new_counts.argmax()])
            votes[top_color] = votes.get(top_color, 0) + 1

    # Choose the colour with the most votes, or -1 if we have no evidence.
    fill = max(votes, key=votes.get) if votes else -1

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Decide which clicks to queue.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    if fill < 0:
        # Fill colour not yet confirmed – probe a single region to gather more data.
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append("fill mechanic unconfirmed -> probe 1 region")
        clicks = paint_plan(frame, max_clicks=1, trace=trace)
    else:
        # Fill colour confirmed – click the largest remaining background regions.
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(f"fill_color={fill} -> fill regions")
        clicks = paint_plan(frame, trace=trace)

    # Queue the determined clicks.
    for (x, y) in clicks:
        act("CLICK", x, y)

def toggle_core(
    current_frame: Any,
    transitions: list[dict[str, Any]],
    act: Callable[..., None],
    trace: list[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Lights‑out core: rebuild click stencils from the observed transitions,
    solve the board over GF(2) and queue the resulting click plan.  If there are
    not yet enough stencils (< _MIN_STENCILS) or no solution is found, queue a
    systematic probe click.

    **Patch rationale**
    The original implementation caps the size of a learned stencil at
    ``_MAX_STENCIL = 12``.  Many toggle games (row/column toggles, large crosses,
    etc.) affect far more cells, causing those transitions to be discarded.
    Consequently the linear system built from the stencils is incomplete and
    often inconsistent, leading to repeated “GF2 inconsistent” messages and a
    stalled solver.

    This patch raises ``_MAX_STENCIL`` to the total number of cells in the
    current board (or a generous fallback) before extracting stencils, ensuring
    that *all* observed click patterns are retained.  With a complete stencil
    set the GF(2) solver can find a valid plan.
    """
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Increase the allowed stencil size before extracting stencils.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    global _MAX_STENCIL
    try:
        # Convert the frame to a NumPy array to obtain its total size.
        frame_arr = np.asarray(current_frame)
        # Use the board size as an upper bound; this guarantees no legitimate
        # stencil is filtered out while keeping the bound reasonable.
        _MAX_STENCIL = max(_MAX_STENCIL, frame_arr.size)
    except Exception:
        # If conversion fails for any reason, fall back to a large constant.
        _MAX_STENCIL = max(_MAX_STENCIL, 1000)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Normal core logic (unchanged apart from the earlier size adjustment).
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    frame = np.asarray(current_frame)
    stencils = _stencils_from_transitions(transitions)

    if len(stencils) >= _MIN_STENCILS:
        plan = _solve_board(frame, stencils, trace)
        if plan:
            if trace is not None:
                trace.append(f"plan={len(plan)} clicks")
            for (x, y) in plan:
                act("CLICK", x, y)
            return

    # Not enough stencils or no solution – probe the next candidate cell.
    probe = _next_probe(frame, set(stencils))
    if probe is not None:
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(
                f"stencils={len(stencils)} (<{_MIN_STENCILS}) -> "
                f"probe ({probe[0]},{probe[1]})"
            )
        act("CLICK", probe[0], probe[1])

def toggle_core(

    GF(2)-solve for a uniform board and queue the plan; if there are not yet
    enough stencils (<_MIN_STENCILS), queue the next systematic probe click.

    The original implementation only avoided re‑probing cells for which a
    stencil had been learned.  On games where a click does not change the board
    (e.g. non‑toggle puzzles or UI elements), no stencil is ever recorded, so the
    same cell is probed repeatedly, leading to an infinite loop.  This patched
    version tracks *all* clicked positions (including those that produced no
    stencil) and excludes them from future probes, allowing the algorithm to
    exhaust the probe space and stop gracefully when no further information can
    be gathered.
    """
    frame = np.asarray(current_frame)

    # Rebuild stencils from observed transitions.
    stencils = _stencils_from_transitions(transitions)

    # Record every cell that has been clicked, regardless of whether a stencil
    # was learned. This prevents the probe logic from repeatedly clicking the
    # same uninformative cell.
    clicked_positions: set[tuple[int, int]] = {
        tuple(t["xy"]) for t in transitions if t.get("xy") is not None
    }

    # If we have enough stencils, attempt to solve the board.
    if len(stencils) >= _MIN_STENCILS:
        plan = _solve_board(frame, stencils, trace)
        if plan:
            if trace is not None:
                trace.append(f"plan={len(plan)} clicks")
            for (x, y) in plan:
                act("CLICK", x, y)
            return

    # Not enough stencils yet – probe a new cell that we have not clicked before.
    probe = _next_probe(frame, clicked_positions)
    if probe is not None:
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(
                f"stencils={len(stencils)} (<{_MIN_STENCILS}) -> "
                f"probe ({probe[0]},{probe[1]})"
            )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

def paint_core(
    current_frame: Any,
    transitions: list[dict[str, Any]],
    act: Callable[..., None],
    trace: list[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Paint/flood core: infer the fill colour from observed click transitions;
    once confirmed, queue clicks filling the largest remaining background regions;
    before it is confirmed, queue one probe click to elicit the mechanic.

    **Patch:** Many flood‑fill games require the player to *select* a colour
    (e.g. by clicking a palette swatch) before clicking on a background region.
    The original implementation inferred the fill colour but never performed
    the selection step, causing clicks on background cells to have no effect
    and the solver to stall.  This patched version first clicks a cell that
    already has the inferred fill colour (if any) to select it, then proceeds
    with the region‑filling clicks.
    """
    # Convert the current frame to a NumPy array for easy processing.
    frame = np.asarray(current_frame)

    # Infer the colour that background cells should be recoloured to.
    fill = _infer_fill_color(transitions)

    # List of (x, y) clicks we will queue this turn.
    clicks: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

    if fill < 0:
        # Fill mechanic not yet confirmed – probe a single background region.
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append("fill mechanic unconfirmed -> probe 1 region")
        clicks = paint_plan(frame, max_clicks=1, trace=trace)
    else:
        # Fill colour has been inferred.  Many games require an explicit colour
        # selection step (e.g. clicking a palette swatch) before flood‑fill works.
        # Look for any pixel that already has the inferred colour and click it
        # to select the colour.  This cell is guaranteed not to be background
        # (background is 0 by default, and fill != 0).
        ys, xs = np.where(frame == fill)
        if len(ys) > 0:
            sel_x, sel_y = int(xs[0]), int(ys[0])
            if trace is not None:
                trace.append(f"select fill_color={fill} at ({sel_x},{sel_y})")
            clicks.append((sel_x, sel_y))
        else:
            # No cell with the inferred colour is visible – we cannot perform a
            # selection click, but we still attempt to fill in case the game does
            # not require an explicit selection step.
            if trace is not None:
                trace.append(f"fill_color={fill} not found in frame -> no select step")

        # After (optionally) selecting the colour, queue clicks to fill the
        # largest remaining background regions.
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(f"fill_color={fill} -> fill regions")
        region_clicks = paint_plan(frame, trace=trace)
        clicks.extend(region_clicks)

    # Queue all determined clicks.
    for (x, y) in clicks:
        act("CLICK", x, y)

def paint_core(
    current_frame: Any,
    transitions: list[dict[str, Any]],
    act: Callable[..., None],
    trace: list[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Paint/flood core: infer the fill colour from observed click transitions;
    once confirmed, queue clicks filling the largest remaining background regions;
    before it is confirmed, queue one probe click to elicit the mechanic.

    **Patch rationale**
    ------------------
    In some levels the background consists of many isolated cells (size‑1
    components).  The original implementation clicks at most ``max_clicks=14``
    cells per turn, which works when the board retains changes across turns.
    However, on levels where the board *resets* after each turn (or after each
    click) the solver repeatedly clicks the same cells, never making progress.
    To avoid this stall we now, after confirming the fill colour, click **all**
    remaining background components in a single call.  This guarantees that the
    level is solved before any reset can occur, while still preserving the
    original behaviour on levels where the board persists.
    """
    # Convert the current frame to a NumPy array for fast processing.
    frame = np.asarray(current_frame)

    # Infer the colour used to fill background cells from observed click
    # transitions.  A negative result means the mechanic is still unknown.
    fill = _infer_fill_color(transitions)

    if fill < 0:
        # Fill mechanic not yet identified – probe a single region to elicit it.
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append("fill mechanic unconfirmed -> probe 1 region")
        clicks = paint_plan(frame, max_clicks=1, trace=trace)
    else:
        # Fill mechanic confirmed.  Determine *all* remaining background
        # components and click each of them in this turn.  This prevents the
        # solver from getting stuck on levels where the board resets after each
        # turn because it ensures the puzzle is solved in a single batch.
        comps = _bg_regions(frame, _BACKGROUND)
        max_clicks = len(comps)  # one click per component (isolated cell)
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(f"fill_color={fill} -> fill all {max_clicks} regions")
        clicks = paint_plan(frame, max_clicks=max_clicks, trace=trace)

    # Queue the generated clicks.
    for (x, y) in clicks:
        act("CLICK", x, y)

    current_frame: Any,
    transitions: list[dict[str, Any]],
    act: Callable[..., None],
    trace: list[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Lights-out core: rebuild click stencils from the observed transitions,
    GF(2)-solve for a uniform board and queue the plan; if there are not yet
    enough stencils (<_MIN_STENCILS), queue the next systematic probe click."""
    frame = np.asarray(current_frame)

    # Reconstruct the toggle stencils from observed click transitions.
    stencils = _stencils_from_transitions(transitions)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # NOTE: The original implementation used `set(stencils)` as the set of
    # already‑clicked cells.  That only includes positions that have yielded a
    # stencil, so before any stencil is learned the set is empty and the probe
    # routine repeatedly selects the same cell.  We now build a set of *all*
    # clicked positions from the transition log, ensuring we never probe a cell
    # twice.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    clicked_positions: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
    for t in transitions:
        xy = t.get("xy")
        if xy is not None:
            # `xy` may be a list or tuple; coerce to ints.
            clicked_positions.add((int(xy[0]), int(xy[1])))

    # If we have enough stencils, try to solve the board (all‑off or all‑on).
    if len(stencils) >= _MIN_STENCILS:
        plan = _solve_board(frame, stencils, trace)
        if plan:
            if trace is not None:
                trace.append(f"plan={len(plan)} clicks")
            for (x, y) in plan:
                act("CLICK", x, y)
            return

    # Not enough stencils (or no solution found): probe the next unclicked cell.
    probe = _next_probe(frame, clicked_positions)
    if probe is not None:
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(
                f"stencils={len(stencils)} (<{_MIN_STENCILS}) -> "
                f"probe ({probe[0]},{probe[1]})"
            )
        act("CLICK", probe[0], probe[1])

def paint_core(
    current_frame: Any,
    transitions: list[dict[str, Any]],
    act: Callable[..., None],
    trace: list[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Paint/flood core (patched).

    The original implementation assumed that the background colour is always ``0``.
    On many games the canvas background is a different colour (e.g. white = 255,
    or any other colour that dominates the frame).  When the background is not
    ``0`` the helper ``_bg_regions`` finds no regions, ``paint_plan`` returns an
    empty click list and the solver repeatedly clicks a fixed probe location
    without ever confirming the fill mechanic – leading to a stall.

    This patch dynamically infers the background colour as the most frequent
    value in the current frame and passes it to both ``_infer_fill_color`` and
    ``paint_plan``.  It also adds a small safety‑net: if ``paint_plan`` still
    yields no clicks (e.g. a completely filled board), we click the centre of
    the frame as a generic probe.  This ensures the solver always generates at
    least one click and can eventually discover the fill colour or other game
    mechanics.
    """
    # Convert the incoming frame to a NumPy array for fast processing.
    frame = np.asarray(current_frame)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1️⃣ Infer the background colour.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Most paint‑type games have a single colour that occupies the majority of
    # the canvas (the “blank” colour).  We compute the mode of the pixel values.
    # ``np.bincount`` works only for non‑negative integers, so we fall back to
    # ``np.unique`` for other dtypes.
    try:
        flat = frame.ravel()
        if flat.dtype.kind in {"i", "u"}:          # integer types
            # Handle possible negative values by offsetting.
            if flat.min() < 0:
                offset = -int(flat.min())
                counts = np.bincount(flat.astype(int) + offset)
                bg_val = int(np.argmax(counts) - offset)
            else:
                counts = np.bincount(flat.astype(int))
                bg_val = int(np.argmax(counts))
        else:
            # For non‑integer dtypes (e.g. float) use the generic mode.
            vals, cnts = np.unique(flat, return_counts=True)
            bg_val = int(vals[np.argmax(cnts)])
    except Exception:
        # As a last resort default to the original constant.
        bg_val = _BACKGROUND

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2️⃣ Infer the fill colour using the (now correct) background.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    fill = _infer_fill_color(transitions, background=bg_val)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3️⃣ Decide which clicks to queue.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    if fill < 0:
        # Fill colour not yet confirmed – probe a single region.
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(f"fill mechanic unconfirmed -> probe 1 region (bg={bg_val})")
        clicks = paint_plan(frame, background=bg_val, max_clicks=1, trace=trace)
    else:
        # Fill colour known – flood the largest remaining background regions.
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(f"fill_color={fill} -> fill regions (bg={bg_val})")
        clicks = paint_plan(frame, background=bg_val, trace=trace)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4️⃣ Fallback: ensure we always click something.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    if not clicks:
        # No background region was found (e.g. board already filled).  Click the
        # centre of the frame as a generic probe – this may trigger a colour
        # selection UI or other game‑specific behaviour.
        h, w = frame.shape[:2]
        cx, cy = w // 2, h // 2
        clicks = [(cx, cy)]
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(f"fallback click at centre ({cx},{cy})")

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5️⃣ Queue the clicks.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    for (x, y) in clicks:
        act("CLICK", x, y)

def toggle_core(
    current_frame: Any,
    transitions: list[dict[str, Any]],
    act: Callable[..., None],
    trace: list[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Lights-out core with support for multi‑colour (mod‑n) toggle games.

    The original binary (GF(2)) solver is retained for 2‑colour boards.
    For boards with more than two colours the solver builds a linear system
    A·x = b (mod n) where n = number of colours and solves it via Gaussian
    elimination over Zₙ.  The plan consists of clicking each learned stencil
    location x[j] times (mod n).  If no solution is found the probe logic is
    unchanged.
    """
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: modular Gaussian elimination (solve A·x = b (mod mod))
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _modular_solve(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray, mod: int) -> np.ndarray | None:
        """Solve A·x = b (mod mod) using Gaussian elimination.
        Returns a solution vector x (length = n_vars) with entries in 0..mod‑1,
        or None if the system is inconsistent."""
        m, n = a.shape
        # Build augmented matrix [A | b]
        aug = np.concatenate([a % mod, b.reshape(-1, 1) % mod], axis=1).astype(np.int64)
        row = 0
        pivot_cols: list[int] = []
        for col in range(n):
            # Find a pivot row with a non‑zero entry that has an inverse modulo mod
            pivot = None
            for r in range(row, m):
                val = int(aug[r, col]) % mod
                if val != 0:
                    try:
                        _ = pow(val, -1, mod)  # test invertibility
                        pivot = r
                        break
                    except ValueError:
                        # Not invertible (e.g. val and mod not coprime); skip
                        continue
            if pivot is None:
                continue  # no usable pivot in this column → free variable
            # Swap pivot row into position `row`
            if pivot != row:
                aug[[row, pivot]] = aug[[pivot, row]]
            # Normalize pivot row so that the pivot element becomes 1
            piv_val = int(aug[row, col]) % mod
            inv = pow(piv_val, -1, mod)
            aug[row] = (aug[row] * inv) % mod
            # Eliminate the current column from all other rows
            for r in range(m):
                if r != row and aug[r, col] != 0:
                    factor = int(aug[r, col]) % mod
                    aug[r] = (aug[r] - factor * aug[row]) % mod
            pivot_cols.append(col)
            row += 1
            if row == m:
                break
        # Consistency check: any all‑zero left side with non‑zero RHS → no solution
        for r in range(m):
            if not aug[r, :n].any() and aug[r, n] != 0:
                return None
        # Back‑substitution: set free variables to 0, solve for pivots
        x = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int64)
        for i, col in enumerate(pivot_cols):
            x[col] = aug[i, n] % mod
        return x

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: solve a multi‑colour board (mod‑n linear system)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _solve_modular(
        frame: np.ndarray,
        stencils: dict[tuple[int, int], set[tuple[int, int]]],
        mod: int,
        trace: list[str] | None,
    ) -> list[tuple[int, int]] | None:
        """Attempt to solve the board for any uniform colour (0..mod‑1).
        Returns the click plan with the fewest total clicks, or None if no
        target yields a solution."""
        colours = np.asarray(frame, dtype=np.int64)
        h, w = colours.shape
        clicks = sorted(stencils)                     # deterministic order
        n_cells = h * w
        n_vars = len(clicks)

        # Build the toggle matrix A (size n_cells × n_vars)
        A = np.zeros((n_cells, n_vars), dtype=np.int64)
        for j, click in enumerate(clicks):
            for (r, c) in stencils[click]:
                if 0 <= r < h and 0 <= c < w:
                    A[r * w + c, j] = (A[r * w + c, j] + 1) % mod

        best_plan: list[tuple[int, int]] | None = None
        best_len: int | None = None

        # Try every possible uniform target colour
        for target in range(mod):
            # Desired change: (target - current) mod mod
            b = ((target - colours.reshape(-1)) % mod).astype(np.int64)
            x = _modular_solve(A, b, mod)
            if x is None:
                if trace is not None:
                    trace.append(f"modular inconsistent for target={target}")
                continue
            # Expand solution vector into an explicit click list
            plan: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
            total_clicks = 0
            for j in range(n_vars):
                cnt = int(x[j] % mod)
                if cnt:
                    total_clicks += cnt
                    plan.extend([(int(clicks[j][0]), int(clicks[j][1]))] * cnt)
            if plan and (best_plan is None or total_clicks < best_len):
                best_plan = plan
                best_len = total_clicks
        return best_plan

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Core logic
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    frame = np.asarray(current_frame)
    stencils = _stencils_from_transitions(transitions)

    # Determine the number of distinct colours present (modulus for the game)
    try:
        ncolors = int(frame.max()) + 1
    except Exception:
        # Fallback – should never happen with a proper numpy array
        ncolors = 2
    if ncolors < 2:
        ncolors = 2

    # If we have gathered enough distinct stencils, attempt to solve
    if len(stencils) >= _MIN_STENCILS:
        if ncolors == 2:
            # Binary (GF(2)) case – original solver
            plan = _solve_board(frame, stencils, trace)
        else:
            # Multi‑colour (mod‑n) case
            plan = _solve_modular(frame, stencils, ncolors, trace)
        if plan:
            if trace is not None:
                trace.append(f"plan={len(plan)} clicks")
            for (x, y) in plan:
                act("CLICK", x, y)
            return

    # No solution found – probe the next un‑clicked cell
    probe = _next_probe(frame, set(stencils))
    if probe is not None:
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(
                f"stencils={len(stencils)} (<{_MIN_STENCILS}) -> "
                f"probe ({probe[0]},{probe[1]})"
            )
        act("CLICK", probe[0], probe[1])

def toggle_core(
    current_frame: Any,
    transitions: list[dict[str, Any]],
    act: Callable[..., None],
    trace: list[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Lights‑out core with improved probing and early‑exit handling.

    * Detects when the board is already uniform (all OFF or all ON) and stops.
    * Tracks *all* clicked coordinates (including those that produced no observable
      change) to avoid repeatedly probing the same cell.
    * If no further probe candidates exist, aborts instead of looping forever.
    """
    # Convert the current frame to a NumPy array for processing.
    frame = np.asarray(current_frame)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1️⃣  Record every coordinate that has been clicked so far, regardless of
    #     whether a stencil was learned from that click.  This prevents the
    #     probe routine from repeatedly selecting the same cell when a click
    #     produces no observable change (len(diff) == 0) or a diff that is too
    #     large to be stored.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    clicked_coords: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
    for t in transitions:
        xy = t.get("xy")
        if xy is not None:
            clicked_coords.add((int(xy[0]), int(xy[1])))

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2️⃣  Re‑build the click‑stencils from the observed transitions.  Only
    #     diffs of size 1‥_MAX_STENCIL are kept (as before).
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    stencils = _stencils_from_transitions(transitions)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3️⃣  Quick uniform‑board check.  If the board is already all OFF or all ON,
    #     there is nothing to do.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    bits, _off, _on = _binarize(frame)
    if bits.min() == bits.max():
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append("board uniform, solved")
        return

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4️⃣  If we have gathered enough stencils, attempt to solve the puzzle.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    if len(stencils) >= _MIN_STENCILS:
        plan = _solve_board(frame, stencils, trace)
        if plan:
            if trace is not None:
                trace.append(f"plan={len(plan)} clicks")
            for (x, y) in plan:
                act("CLICK", x, y)
            return

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5️⃣  Not enough information yet – probe the next un‑clicked cell.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    probe = _next_probe(frame, clicked_coords)
    if probe is not None:
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(
                f"stencils={len(stencils)} (<{_MIN_STENCILS}) -> "
                f"probe ({probe[0]},{probe[1]})"
            )
        act("CLICK", probe[0], probe[1])
    else:
        # No remaining candidates; abort to avoid an infinite loop.
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append("no more probe candidates, aborting")
        return

def paint_core(
    current_frame: Any,
    transitions: list[dict[str, Any]],
    act: Callable[..., None],
    trace: list[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Paint/flood core with improved stall handling.

    * Infer the fill colour from observed click transitions.
    * If the fill colour is not yet confirmed, probe a background region.
    * After a few consecutive no‑change clicks, fall back to a random
      untried background cell to avoid getting stuck on the same location.
    * When the fill colour is confirmed, click the largest remaining
      background regions, but never repeat a coordinate that has already
      been clicked.
    """
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: collect all coordinates that have already been clicked.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    visited: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
    for t in transitions:
        xy = t.get("xy")
        if xy is not None:
            # xy is a list [x, y]; store as a tuple for fast lookup.
            visited.add((int(xy[0]), int(xy[1])))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: count how many recent clicks produced no visual change.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    consecutive_no_change = 0
    for t in reversed(transitions):
        if t.get("xy") is None:
            continue
        before = np.asarray(t["before"])
        after = np.asarray(t["after"])
        if before.shape != after.shape:
            continue
        if (before != after).any():
            break
        consecutive_no_change += 1

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Infer the fill colour (may be -1 if not yet known).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    fill = _infer_fill_color(transitions)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Convert the current frame to a NumPy array for region analysis.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    frame = np.asarray(current_frame)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Decide which clicks to queue.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    clicks: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

    if fill < 0:
        # Fill colour not yet confirmed → probing mode.
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append("fill mechanic unconfirmed -> probe region")
        # Ask paint_plan for a single candidate (largest background region).
        candidate_clicks = paint_plan(frame, max_clicks=1, trace=trace)
        # Discard any candidate that we have already tried.
        clicks = [(x, y) for (x, y) in candidate_clicks if (x, y) not in visited]

        # If we have no fresh candidate (or we have repeatedly failed),
        # fall back to a random untried background cell.
        if not clicks or consecutive_no_change >= 5:
            # Locate all background cells.
            bg_mask = frame == _BACKGROUND
            bg_coords = np.argwhere(bg_mask)  # each row: [row, col]
            # Filter out cells we have already clicked.
            untried = [
                (int(col), int(row))
                for row, col in bg_coords
                if (int(col), int(row)) not in visited
            ]
            if untried:
                rng = np.random.default_rng()
                idx = rng.integers(len(untried))
                clicks = [untried[idx]]
            else:
                # No untried background cells left – give up this step.
                clicks = []
    else:
        # Fill colour confirmed → normal filling mode.
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(f"fill_color={fill} -> fill regions")
        candidate_clicks = paint_plan(frame, trace=trace)
        # Remove any clicks that have already been attempted.
        clicks = [(x, y) for (x, y) in candidate_clicks if (x, y) not in visited]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Queue the determined clicks.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for (x, y) in clicks:
        act("CLICK", x, y)

def toggle_core(
    current_frame: Any,
    transitions: list[dict[str, Any]],
    act: Callable[..., None],
    trace: list[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Lights-out core: rebuild click stencils from the observed transitions,
    GF(2)-solve for a uniform board and queue the plan; if there are not yet
    enough stencils (<_MIN_STENCILS), queue the next systematic probe click.

    Fixed: previously the probe logic could repeatedly click the same cell
    when a click produced no observable change (i.e., no stencil).  Such
    clicks were not recorded in ``stencils`` and thus were not considered
    “clicked”, causing ``_next_probe`` to return the same coordinate
    indefinitely.  The fix tracks all attempted clicks (including those
    with zero effect) via the transition history and passes this combined
    set to ``_next_probe`` to avoid re‑probing already tried cells.
    """
    frame = np.asarray(current_frame)

    # Reconstruct stencils from transitions where a change was observed.
    stencils = _stencils_from_transitions(transitions)

    # Record all attempted click positions (including those that caused no change).
    attempted_clicks: set[tuple[int, int]] = {
        tuple(t["xy"]) for t in transitions if t.get("xy") is not None
    }

    # Combine with positions for which we have a stencil; this set is used to
    # avoid probing the same cell again.
    clicked = set(stencils) | attempted_clicks

    # If we have enough distinct stencils, try to solve the board.
    if len(stencils) >= _MIN_STENCILS:
        plan = _solve_board(frame, stencils, trace)
        if plan:
            if trace is not None:
                trace.append(f"plan={len(plan)} clicks")
            for (x, y) in plan:
                act("CLICK", x, y)
            return

    # Not enough stencils yet (or no solution found); probe a new cell.
    probe = _next_probe(frame, clicked)
    if probe is not None:
        if trace is not None:
            trace.append(
                f"stencils={len(stencils)} (<{_MIN_STENCILS}) -> "
                f"probe ({probe[0]},{probe[1]})"
            )
        act("CLICK", probe[0], probe[1])
